content.glance: BNS s. 229 — Punishment for false evidence.

sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body:
229. (1) Whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any stage of a judicial proceeding, or fabricates false evidence for the purpose of being used in any stage of a judicial proceeding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees
(2) Whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any case other than that referred to in sub-section (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to five thousand rupees

sections.heading: Essential ingredients
sections.body:
(1) Whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any stage of a judicial proceeding, or fabricates false evidence for the purpose of being used in any stage of a judicial proceeding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees
(2) Whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any case other than that referred to in sub-section
(1), shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to five thousand rupees

sections.heading: Statutory illustrations
sections.body:
A, in an enquiry before a Magistrate for the purpose of ascertaining whether Z ought to be committed for trial, makes on oath a statement which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of a judicial proceeding, A has given false evidence
A, in an enquiry before an officer deputed by a Court to ascertain on the spot the boundaries of land, makes on oath a statement which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of a judicial proceeding, A has given false evidence

sections.heading: Explanations
sections.body:
Explanation 1.—A trial before a Court-martial is a judicial proceeding
Explanation 2.—An investigation directed by law preliminary to a proceeding before a Court, is a stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place before a Court
Explanation 3.—An investigation directed by a Court according to law, and conducted under the authority of a Court, is a stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place before a Court

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 229 constitutes a key component of Chapter XIV (Of False Evidence and Offences against Public Justice) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing punishment for false evidence. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of punishment for false evidence under Section 229 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 229.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 229 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 229 vs General Attempt: Section 229 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XIV; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 229 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 229 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of False Evidence and Offences against Public Justice.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 229 for conduct relating to punishment for false evidence.
Rule: Under BNS s. 229, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 229.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 229 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
